scope: Prove that the real installed KDE Kicker application search accepts keyboard input without clicking the field and filters a unique app entry; retain the private panel open/close checks.

method.environment: Private Plasma/KWin/Xvfb session with disposable XDG homes, current installed Kicker QML copied and instrumented privately, current DomainOS application applet/panel, private D-Bus runtime under ~/tempia.
method.search_entry: One artificial desktop entry named R636UniqueSearchMarker, visible only in disposable XDG_DATA_HOME.
method.input: The native Kicker search field had activeFocus before any field click; QTest sent each character to its QWindow. Search text was observed, category root list became hidden, runner results became visible, and exactly one matching result was counted.
method.cleanup: The result reports own_daemons_stopped=true, private_host_exited_cleanly=true, qml_runtime_errors_zero=true.

fixture_limits: Private Plasma/KWin/Xvfb fixture; not the live plasmashell panel or the user desktop.
The search application is synthetic and is not launched.
Human visual acceptance of the live menu and drawer remains pending.
conclusion: The Kicker search field was focused before input, accepted the typed unique name without a field click, switched to result mode, and returned exactly one matching artificial application. The existing same-button menu toggles also passed in the private panel fixture. No production change is indicated by this proof.
next: Keep P01 at waiting_user. The user should inspect Applications search without clicking its field and verify menu/drawer repeated-click behavior in the live lsi desktop.
